requirements.evidence: All task and contract items are present: locale/name pins (`.env.example:1,9`, `phpunit.xml:22-24`), the `pegafila` Markdown theme (`config/mail.php:129-130`) with `#0f7490` on the button variants (`resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-242`), pt-BR subjects (`lang/pt_BR.json:559,804`), guest-only reset routes (`routes/web.php:15-26`) implemented in `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:29-85` (always `passwords.sent`, full password rules, remember_token rotation, `PasswordReset` event, redirect to `/`), and the auth/signed/throttled verification route and controller (`routes/web.php:30`, `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:14-32`) that 403s on an id or hash mismatch.

conventions.evidence: Mostly Laravel-native and consistent with siblings, but `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:60-68` validates three fields with nested password rules inline instead of the Form Request the conventions require beyond one or two fields, and no `CHANGELOG.md` entry was added. `$fillable` is deliberately preserved (`app/Models/User.php:13`). The missing tests are scored under the tests dimension.

security.evidence: Every input is validated server-side (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:31-33,60-68`), all output is escaped (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:5-8`, `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:3-16`), the request endpoint always returns the same `passwords.sent` status without revealing whether the address exists (`PasswordResetController.php:35-41`), verification uses `hash_equals` and aborts 403 (`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:18-24`) behind `auth`+`signed` (`routes/web.php:30`), and the sensitive endpoints are throttled (`routes/web.php:20,30`); no secrets or unescaped user input.

tests.evidence: There are no `tests/` hunks anywhere in `change.diff`; the forgot/reset routes, the verification controller, the two views, the pt-BR mail rendering and the theme all ship with zero Pest/PHPUnit coverage. This is the rubric's lowest anchor: no tests for the new behavior.

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses Laravel's `Password` broker, stock notifications and the default mail theme rather than bespoke code. Minor redundancy: `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:35-38` queries the user and then `Password::sendResetLink()` repeats the lookup, and `resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:3-5` adds `request()` fallbacks the controller always pre-empts.

readability.evidence: Short, single-purpose methods with docblocks (`app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:29-85`), descriptive route names (`routes/web.php:15-30`), small labelled forms (`resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:6-11`), and no dead code, debug output or inconsistent style.

scope.evidence: Every hunk serves the task: locale pins (`.env.example:1,9`, `phpunit.xml:22-24`), mail config and theme (`config/mail.php:129-130`, `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css`), lang keys (`lang/pt_BR.json:559,804`), two controllers, two views and five routes. No login, registration, `/home`, Livewire, layout or other out-of-scope features were added.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for the password-reset request/update flow, the signed verification endpoint, the two views or the pt-BR/theme mail rendering, violating the project's mandatory 'no production code without a test' rule for auth-critical behavior.
The conventions require a Keep a Changelog entry under `[Unreleased]` for every change, and none was added.
`update()` validates three fields with nested password rules inline; the conventions reserve inline validation for one or two fields and require a Form Request once rules grow beyond that.
`store()` looks up the user and then `Password::sendResetLink()` performs the same lookup again, so the extra query is redundant.

The view falls back to `request()->route('token')` and `request()->query('email')` even though `PasswordResetController::edit()` always passes `$token` and `$email`, adding unnecessary defensive code.

review.summary: The change adds the pt-BR password-reset request/update flow, the signed e-mail verification endpoint, the PegaFila Markdown mail theme and the missing subject translations in small, security-conscious Laravel-native code. It ships with no tests at all, plus a missing CHANGELOG entry and inline three-field validation as secondary convention issues, so it needs changes before merging.
